findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_txt, decode_bounce, analyze_dmarc_report, analyze_email_headers · Private data: check_spf, check_dkim, discover_dkim, check_dmarc, check_tls_rpt, check_mta_sts, check_bimi, check_dane, check_m365, check_dns_propagation, check_txt, decode_bounce, analyze_dmarc_report, check_website, check_mcp_keys · Public sink: check_mx, check_dns_propagation, decode_bounce, analyze_email_headers · Destructive: check_m365, check_google_workspace.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_txt, decode_bounce, analyze_dmarc_report, analyze_email_headers · Private data: check_spf, check_dkim, discover_dkim, check_dmarc, check_tls_rpt, check_mta_sts, check_bimi, check_dane, check_m365, check_dns_propagation, check_txt, decode_bounce, analyze_dmarc_report, check_website, check_mcp_keys · Public sink: check_mx, check_dns_propagation, decode_bounce, analyze_email_headers · Destructive: check_m365, check_google_workspace

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
